text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports anxiety, now improved, and a breast lump that persists but is smaller.
- history of present illness: the patient started buspirone (prescribed by a prior clinician) and had severe anxiety in November and December, possibly linked to stress from COVID-19 work, stopping a birth control pill, and progesterone use. Anxiety has since settled. Lumps in the breast are smaller but persist, with mild tenderness. The patient has a family history of breast cancer (mother, diagnosed near age 45).
- physical examination: palpable small bumps in the neck; a slightly denser, tender area in one breast; skin exam of the genital/itching area was reviewed and looked fine.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: severe anxiety, irritability, increased hunger, breast tenderness, persistent breast lumps, and itching or discomfort in the genital area (improved with cream).
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: buspirone (dosage N/A), new prescription from another clinician; the patient stopped a birth control pill (Camila).
- follow-up instructions: continue monitoring the breast lumps; referral to a breast specialist, who will call to schedule within a few business days; repeat Pap test.
